title: 37.8 A 13.5µW 35-Keyword End-to-End Keyword Spotting System Featuring Personalized On-Chip Training in 28nm CMOS
problem: Existing keyword spotting systems recognize only up to 10 keywords with low accuracy for accented speakers, and lack user-specific trainability, limiting personalization for diverse speech patterns and larger vocabularies.
motivation: Consumer devices require personalized KWS supporting 35+ keywords with high accuracy across diverse accents while minimizing power consumption during both inference and training.
method: The system uses a tiny AI model (a convolutional neural network, or CNN) small enough to fit on a single chip. It learns directly from each person's voice on-chip—not on external servers—which enables personalization while saving power. To minimize power consumption to 13.5 microwatts, it uses two techniques: a simplified approach to identifying important sound patterns (called feature extraction) using sine waves and approximate logarithms, and quantization (using lower-precision numbers to reduce power and space needs). This enables accurate recognition of 35 keywords, even with accented speakers, while adapting to each user's unique speech patterns.
key_novelty: The core idea is personalizing the system by training it directly on-chip—using simplified math based on sine waves and approximate logarithms—to achieve ultra-low power recognition of 35 keywords even with accented speech, consuming just 13.5 microwatts.
contributions: 35-keyword KWS system supporting 9 different accent profiles
Sine-based convolution with approximate logarithm for low-complexity feature extraction
primary_theme: Low-power personalized multi-keyword speech spotting with on-chip training
